dates.notes: Sixth ministerial meeting of the U.S.–EU Trade and Technology Council, Leuven, 4–5 April 2024; the joint statement was published on 5 April 2024. The first technical Dialogue under the commitment was held on 11 July 2024. No TTC ministerial or joint statement after the September 2024 stock-taking was located; the European Commission's fact page is titled '(2021-2024)' and its TTC topic page is marked archived. No later meeting of the AI-safety Dialogue was located.

gaps: No standalone US–EU AI-safety agreement, MOU, administrative arrangement or terms of reference was located.
The AI-safety commitment is one section of a broad TTC joint statement covering many non-AI issues; only the AI section was analysed.
The joint statement creates no binding obligations, ratification, depositary, monitoring, reporting or dispute settlement.

No TTC ministerial, joint statement or working-group output after the September 2024 stock-taking was located; the Commission presents the TTC as a 2021-2024 framework and archives its topic page, but no formal closure decision was located.
No meeting of the AI-safety Dialogue after 11 July 2024 was located on official EU or US pages.
The August 2025 US-EU trade framework provides for 'setting up a Digital Dialogue'; the Commission described it on 29 June 2026 as a potential future dialogue, and no launch document was located.
Only the English versions were read; other language versions were not checked.
The separate U.S.–EU Administrative Arrangement on AI and computing is not catalogued as an AI-safety agreement.

languages.note: English versions published by the European Commission and the U.S. Trade Representative were read. Other language versions were not checked; there is no authentic-language clause because the instrument is not a treaty.

provenance.discovered_via: European Commission and USTR TTC pages; NIST and European Commission technical-dialogue pages.

related.note: Parallel transatlantic AI-safety cooperation in 2024; the UK–US instrument is an MOU, while the US–EU side is a political dialogue commitment.
The TTC statement places the AI-safety dialogue in the wider international AI-safety process.
The joint statement refers to coordinating contributions to the OECD, among other multilateral fora.

ai_provisions: The parties reaffirm a risk-based approach to AI and coordination in the G7, OECD, G20, Council of Europe and UN processes.
Leaders from the European AI Office and the U.S. AI Safety Institute briefed one another on their approaches and mandates.
The two institutions 'committed to establishing a Dialogue' to deepen collaboration and foster scientific information exchange on benchmarks, potential risks and future technological trends.
The cooperation is linked to the Joint Roadmap on Evaluation and Measurement Tools for Trustworthy AI and Risk Management and to interoperable international standards.
The parties encourage advanced AI developers to apply the Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct.
relevance.excluded_scope: The joint statement is broad — trade, technology, standards, economic security and human rights. Only the AI-related commitments are catalogued. There is no standalone AI-safety agreement, MOU, administrative arrangement, binding obligation, ratification or dispute settlement.
relevance.reason: The AI section of the sixth U.S.–EU Trade and Technology Council joint statement records a political commitment by the European AI Office and the U.S. AI Safety Institute to establish a Dialogue for scientific information exchange on benchmarks, potential risks and future technological trends. It is not a standalone US–EU AI-safety MOU, administrative arrangement or treaty; no separate terms of reference or binding text was located. The record catalogues the joint statement because it is the primary source of the commitment.

status_note: Political joint statement, not a treaty. The AI-safety commitment is the establishment of a Dialogue between the European AI Office and the U.S. AI Safety Institute. No standalone US–EU AI-safety MOU, administrative arrangement or terms of reference was located. The separate U.S.–EU Administrative Arrangement on AI and computing is a research-cooperation instrument, not an AI-safety agreement. The joint statement creates no binding obligations, ratification, depositary or dispute settlement. No TTC ministerial or joint statement after the September 2024 stock-taking was located; the Commission presents the TTC as a 2021-2024 framework and archives its topic page, without a formal closure decision. No later meeting of the AI-safety Dialogue was located.
